classification: synthetic local capacity, exact-alias deduplication, integrity, and latency evidence; not vulnerability-detection evidence

environment.storage: NVMe Btrfs under /home with zstd:1 compression

method.database_per_size: fresh local SQLite catalog removed after its result row
method.input_class: deterministic generated synthetic OSV-shaped records; no real vulnerability labels
method.exact_alias_policy: every tenth source record aliases the immediately preceding synthetic CVE, yielding an expected 10 percent source-record reduction
method.query_cache_state: same-process after ingestion; warm or partially warm and order-dependent

row_semantics.canonical_vulnerabilities_schema_field: exact-alias canonical rows; the historical schema field name does not mean human-validated vulnerabilities

process_measurement.scope: one direct benchmark process covering both sizes; not per-size peak memory

build_and_run_process_measurement.command_class: cargo 1.92.0 release build and benchmark run in one measured process tree
build_and_run_process_measurement.scope: includes Cargo and compilation/linking work as well as execution; it is a conservative pipeline observation and not catalog runtime RSS

measured_query_bottleneck.query: broad FTS phrase present in every synthetic source row with a result limit of 20
measured_query_bottleneck.comparison: FTS was the measured query bottleneck; exact identifier and exact package medians stayed below 0.3 milliseconds in the retained direct run

real_source_reference_lane.note: Real-source provenance and counts are retained separately; the M0.3 timing rows are synthetic and do not relabel these source records as validated vulnerabilities.

limitations: The 50k and 100k rows are synthetic source-record capacity tests, not counts of real or human-validated vulnerabilities.
The exact 10 percent alias pattern validates deterministic structural deduplication only; it does not measure semantic deduplication precision or recall.
Query medians use five same-process samples after ingestion and are warm or partially warm; cold-start, p95, p99, and concurrent query latency remain unmeasured.
The two sizes ran sequentially in one process, so filesystem cache and order effects prevent treating them as independent trials.
The process-wide peak RSS covers both sizes and cannot be attributed to either row.
The 571,660 KiB build-and-run peak includes compiler and linker memory; the direct benchmark process peak was 100,552 KiB, and neither is a per-size peak.
Crash recovery under load, concurrent writers, low-power hardware, and five to twenty million relationships remain unmeasured.
